rubrics.criterion: The dedicated, never-reachable entities of the abandoned dry-run experiment are all removed from the implementation translation unit: the per-family capacity estimators (manifest entries E4, E5, E6), the dry-run wrapper over the core formatting engine (E7), and the file-scope result-accounting state (E2). No such helper or module-level state survives anywhere in the library.
rubrics.rationale: This case is built as one parked truncation-safe formatting experiment whose scaffolding was never reachable from the public API at any point; these are the self-contained sites the whole task turns on, and leaving even one keeps the abandoned experiment alive in the shipped tree.

rubrics.criterion: The live formatting functions are restored to their pre-experiment form: the integer formatting stage (E8), the float conversion (E9), and the core format-parsing loop (E10) no longer declare the length-accounting local, no accounting store remains in any of them, and the disabled debug emission guarded behind a permanently false condition is gone from the parse loop. The remaining code is the original conversion and parsing logic with no leftover instrumentation.
rubrics.rationale: The experiment instrumented three live, hot code paths of the formatting engine; the requested cleanup is judged complete only when every trace of that instrumentation - variable, stores, and dead branch - is excised without altering the surrounding conversion logic.

rubrics.criterion: The removal follows the experiment's reference chain to its end: the counting callback compatible with the live output-sink signature (E3), whose only reference was the abandoned dry-run wrapper (E7) and which therefore merely appeared busy, is removed along with (or as a consequence of) the wrapper; and the patch strands nothing new, i.e. removing the experiment leaves no residual code whose only purpose or reference was part of what was removed.
rubrics.rationale: This instance deliberately hides one layer of the abandoned experiment behind another: the counting sink looks like part of the live output plumbing until the dead wrapper around it goes. A repair that only takes the directly visible pieces leaves exactly this masked sink behind, which is the coordination obligation this rubric grades.

rubrics.criterion: The public header again declares exactly the library's shipped and implemented API: the prototype of the planned length-query entry point (E1) and the documentation block that was drafted for it are removed, so no declared function is left without an implementation.
rubrics.rationale: The parked experiment seeded its API surface in the public header before the implementation existed. That orphan declaration is part of the abandoned work product this instance asks to sweep, it misleads every library user about available functionality, and it sits outside the compiled unit, so nothing but a deliberate cleanup decision removes it.

rubrics.criterion: No narration of the abandoned experiment survives in comments: the notes about the truncation-safe accounting, dry-run plans, and issue #45 reporting that were attached to the removed or surrounding code are not left behind on code that ships.
rubrics.rationale: The modeled developer documented the half-finished plan in comments at every junction, so comment residue is the soft remainder of the abandoned experiment in this instance; a sweep that removes the code but keeps its narration leaves the tree still telling readers about a mechanism that no longer exists.

rubrics.criterion: The cleanup deletes live machinery that the abandoned experiment merely referenced - for example the string-length helper or the character-output sinks - or otherwise edits live conversion, output, or engine code beyond deleting the experiment's own instrumentation.
rubrics.rationale: Several stranded pieces deliberately reference genuine library primitives and mimic the live output plumbing to appear busy; the instance's failure mode is a sweep that treats those live collaborators as part of the experiment. The boundary the task draws is reachability of the experiment, not adjacency to it.

rubrics.criterion: While clearing the experiment, the repair changes the library's shipped contracts or their implementation logic beyond pure subtraction - for example rewiring, renaming, or 'improving' the documented behavior or return semantics of the public formatting functions, including the truncation-reporting semantics settled for issue #45, instead of only removing the abandoned instrumentation.
rubrics.rationale: The accounting stores sit millimeters away from the issue #45 return-value bookkeeping in the core engine, so a plausible incomplete repair path is to rework the surrounding semantics under the guise of cleanup. The task asks for the library back exactly as it should have been, with only the experiment subtracted.
